answer: Rather than count keys, the protocol charges every seat a live retrieval tax. Each agent is one point on a shared atlas of registered seats; each epoch a beacon names a slot in a vast sable index of one-time secrets. The agent has ninety seconds to fetch its own slot and re-sign, and other slots stay dark. Proxying fails: N sybil seats mean N independent sessions burning real compute in the same window, and a duplicate-read detector slashes any cluster sharing one cache. So the attacker pays a machine plus a bond per seat, pushing margin to its nadir right where sybils would otherwise pay.
